identity.name: Omani Empire (East African coast)
alt_names: African dominion of the Sultan of Muscat

land.text: the Tanzanian and Kenyan coast that Cliopatria draws inside its Sultanate of Oman shapes from 1744 to 1814

predecessors.note: Cliopatria carries the African coast inside the 'Sultanate of Oman' row until 1814 (shapes.csv lists Tanzania and Kenya for sultanate-of-oman_1744 to _1812) and as this separate row from 1814. No page opened dates a change in 1814.

land.text: the African section of the empire, 'ruled by Majid bin Said' as the Sultanate of Zanzibar after the division of 1856

successors.note: Cliopatria's People's Republic of Zanzibar row (1856-1889) is the Sultanate of Zanzibar. The Omani homeland went to Thuwaini bin Said's Sultanate of Muscat and Oman (sultanate-of-oman).

capitals.name: Muscat
capitals.note: The sultan's seat outside the African land. The Omani Empire infobox gives 'Muscat (1792-1832); Zanzibar (1832-1856)'; the Said bin Sultan page dates the move to 1840.

capitals.name: Zanzibar (Stone Town)
capitals.note: 'In 1840, Said moved his capital from Muscat to Stone Town in Zanzibar'; the Omani Empire infobox says 1832.

rulers.name: Said bin Sultan (Sayyid Said)
rulers.title: Sultan of Muscat and Oman
rulers.note: Omani Empire infobox: 'Said bin Sultan 1806-1856'. The Said bin Sultan page gives his death as 19 October 1856 in the infobox and a reign ending 4 June 1856 in its lead. Only the reign that overlaps the dossier is listed. [Reviewer af-05, 2026-10-19: span clipped to the dossier's life, which starts in 1814.]

minus.text: Mombasa and its mainland, a radius of the size of the hole Cliopatria leaves in 1824-1827

correction.text: the coast from Cape Delgado to Lamu with Zanzibar, Pemba and Mafia, without Mombasa, which the Mazrui hold outside Omani rule until 1837

keyframe_review.note: 64,591 km2 for 1814-1823, bbox Cape Delgado to Lamu, including Mombasa. The Mombasa page has the town independent from 1746 ('the last of them made it independent again (disputed by Oman)') under the Mazrui sultans, among them 'Abdallah ibn Ahmad 1812-1823; it names no Mazrui land beyond Mombasa, so the cut is Cliopatria's own 1824 hole (10 cells, 39.25-39.66 E, 3.85-4.27 S). The rest of the strip is unverified: the Omani Empire infobox gives no area and no page opened dates an Omani hold on Lamu or the northern coast before 1843 (Lamu supplied troops to Said in 1844, Pate page). The shape stops at Lamu; Pate Island, Siyu and Faza lie outside it.

61,916 km2 for 1824-1827: the same strip with a 10-cell hole at Mombasa. Mombasa page: 'From 9 February 1824 to 25 July 1826, there was a British protectorate over Mombasa', after which 'Omani rule was restored in 1826; seven liwalis where appointed'. The Said bin Sultan page nevertheless has Said 'conquer Mombasa' only in 1837 and the Mombasa page has the 24 June 1837 'nominal' annexation, so the hole is kept for 1826 and 1827: the Fort Jesus page has the fort under 'local rule from 1741 to 1837' and the ledger draws Mombasa as an Omani vassal from 1826 and annexed in 1837 (see notes).

minus.text: Mombasa and its mainland, a radius of the size of the hole Cliopatria leaves in 1824-1827

correction.text: the coast from Cape Delgado to Lamu with Zanzibar, Pemba and Mafia, without Mombasa, which the Mazrui hold outside Omani rule until 1837

keyframe_review.note: 64,591 km2 for 1828-1839: Cliopatria returns Mombasa to Oman in 1828. The pages opened date the Omani annexation of Mombasa to 24 June 1837 ('nominally annexed by Said bin Sultan' on the Mombasa page; 'In 1837, he conquered Mombasa' on the Said bin Sultan page); the Mombasa page also lists Omani liwalis from 1826. Taking the two dated 1837 statements, the shape holds without Mombasa for 1828-1836 (the Fort Jesus page: 'The fort fell under local rule from 1741 to 1837... when it was again captured by the Omanis'), with an Omani vassal tint over it from 1826 in the ledger, and the full shape begins in the new keyframe of 1837.

correction.text: the Cape Delgado-Lamu coast with Zanzibar, Pemba, Mafia and Mombasa: 'the empire's African dominion extended along the Swahili coast to 12 miles south of the Ruvuma River'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1837-1839: the full Cliopatria 1828 strip, Mombasa included, after the annexation of 24 June 1837.

correction.text: the 1837-1839 strip from Cape Delgado to Lamu with Zanzibar, Pemba, Mafia and Mombasa, held directly; the Banadir coast of Somalia is a nominal dependency drawn as a vassal in the ledger

keyframe_review.note: 185,340 km2 for 1840-1852, bbox 14.6 S to 12.0 N: the strip plus the Mozambican coast down to 14.6 S and the whole Somali coast up to Cape Guardafui. The Omani Empire page says the African dominion 'extended along the Swahili coast to 12 miles south of the Ruvuma River' (the Ruvuma mouth is at about 10.5 S), so the Mozambican coast beyond Cape Delgado is not supported; the Banadir coast is only a nominal dependency ('In 1843 he nominated a nominal representative in Mogadishu', Said bin Sultan page; Mogadishu bombarded in 1828; the Banadir allotted to Zanzibar only at the 1856 division) and goes in the vassal tint of the ledger, not in the shape. The Pate and Siyu coast, outside the shape, was in revolt from 1843 (see the ledger). The page gives no area.

correction.text: the strip from Cape Delgado to Lamu with Zanzibar, Pemba, Mafia and Mombasa, held directly; the Banadir coast a nominal dependency drawn as a vassal in the ledger

keyframe_review.note: 185,340 km2 for 1853-1855, the same shape as 1840 and wrong in the same way (Mozambique to 14.6 S, Somalia to Cape Guardafui); the same correction applies. No page opened dates a change in 1853.

region.text: the coast from Cape Delgado to Lamu with Zanzibar, Pemba and Mafia (Cliopatria's first shape)

ledger.note: 1814: the Omani coast of East Africa appears as its own dominion. Cliopatria starts the row in 1814; none of the pages opened dates an event in that year. The Omani hold on the coast goes back to the capture of Fort Jesus (infobox 'Occupation of Fort Jesus by Saif bin Sultan: 1696'; Mombasa page 'the capture of Fort Jesus in 1698').

region.text: Mombasa under liwalis appointed from Muscat

ledger.note: 25 July 1826: the British protectorate over Mombasa ends and Omani rule is restored through liwalis. 'From 9 February 1824 to 25 July 1826, there was a British protectorate over Mombasa'; 'Omani rule was restored in 1826; seven liwalis where appointed'; the infobox has Mombasa under the Sultanate of Zanzibar from 1826. The Fort Jesus page and the Said bin Sultan page still have local rule until 1837, so the relation is drawn as a vassal tint, not as annexation.

region.text: Mogadishu and the Banadir coast, where Said had a nominal representative

ledger.note: 1828: the Banadir suzerainty is restored. Omani Empire page: 'Thus Mogadishu was bombarded by Omani forces in 1828 and the Banadir Omani suzerainty was restored.' Later the Said bin Sultan page: 'In 1843 he nominated a nominal representative in Mogadishu' and 'was forced to pay tribute to Sultan Yusuf Mahamud Ibrahim' of the Geledi, so the claim stayed a thin suzerainty. The Banadir was allotted to the Sultan of Zanzibar at the 1856 division (Omani Empire page). [Reviewer af-05, 2026-10-19: year moved from 1843 to the 1828 of the Omani Empire page.]
June 1837: the vassal relation ends in annexation (see the gain below).

region.text: Mombasa, last held by the Mazrui sultan Sulayman ibn 'Ali (1823-1826) and his successors

ledger.note: 1837: Said bin Sultan takes Mombasa. 'On 24 June 1837, it was nominally annexed by Said bin Sultan of Muscat and Oman' (Mombasa page); 'In 1837, he conquered Mombasa' (Said bin Sultan page). The Fort Jesus page agrees: local rule 1741-1837, then 'again captured by the Omanis'. The Omani liwalis the Mombasa page lists from 1826 are the vassal tint above.
1840: Said bin Sultan moves his capital from Muscat to Stone Town, Zanzibar ('In 1840, Said moved his capital from Muscat to Stone Town in Zanzibar'); the Omani Empire infobox says 1832.

region.text: Pate Island with Siyu and Faza, the Pate sultanate's towns (coordinates are the researcher's reading; the gazetteer lacks Pate, Siyu and Faza)

ledger.note: January 1844: Said's army lands at Faza against Siyu and Pate. The Sheikh of Siyu and the new Sheikh of Pate repudiated Said's authority in 1843; an army of about 2,000 under Amir Hemed 'landed at Faza in January 1844', was ambushed near Siyu and withdrew after three weeks without a victory.

region.text: Pate Island with Siyu and Faza, the Pate sultanate's towns (coordinates are the researcher's reading; the gazetteer lacks Pate, Siyu and Faza)

ledger.note: 1845: Siyu defeats Said again. 'In 1845 Siyu gave Seyyid Said one of his greatest military defeats'; Amir Hemed was killed. Siyu submitted to Zanzibar only in 1863 (Pate page), so the fighting ends with the Omani failure.

region.text: the African section 'ruled by Majid bin Said'

ledger.note: 19 October 1856: the Omani Empire is divided between Said's sons. Majid bin Said becomes Sultan of Zanzibar, 'obliged to pay an annual tribute to the Omani court in Muscat'; Thuwaini bin Said takes Muscat and Oman. The Omani Empire page: 'In 1856 the Omani Empire was divided' (infobox 'Division of the Omani Empire: 1856'). The month is from the Sultanate of Zanzibar infobox.

wars.name: Omani bombardment of Mogadishu
wars.outcome: Omani suzerainty over the Banadir restored: 'Thus Mogadishu was bombarded by Omani forces in 1828 and the Banadir Omani suzerainty was restored', after an incident in 1823 in which two community leaders aboard an Omani ship were kidnapped.
wars.note: The page records mutual suspicion between the Omani rulers and Mogadishu in the 1820s; the restored suzerainty is the ledger's vassal_start of 1828, not a change of direct rule, so the war has no zone. [Reviewer af-05, 2026-10-19: outcome corrected to the page's sentence.]

wars.name: Omani expedition against Siyu and Pate

zones.text: Pate Island with Siyu and Faza, the Pate sultanate's towns (coordinates are the researcher's reading; the gazetteer lacks Pate, Siyu and Faza)

wars.outcome: Failure: a force of about 2,000 landed at Faza in January 1844 and withdrew without a victory; Amir Hemed was killed at Siyu in 1845. Siyu submitted to Zanzibar only in 1863.

certainty.note: The coast is a string of towns and claims: no treaty or survey fixes a boundary in the pages opened. The southern limit 'to 12 miles south of the Ruvuma River' is the nearest thing to a stated frontier.

sources.note: Fort built 1593-1596; Sultan Yusuf ibn al-Hasan took it in 1631, Portuguese back 1632; Omani siege 1696-1698; Portuguese again 1728-1729; local rule 1741-1837; Omani capture 1837.

notes:
Cliopatria's row 'Omani Slave Coast' (1814-1855) is the East African dominion of the Sultans of Muscat and Oman, the 'Omani Empire' of Wikipedia (the title Cliopatria gives, 'Omanis', is the article on the people). The dossier is named for the state, with the Cliopatria label kept as an alias.

Rows to settle: (1) The coast is inside Cliopatria's 'Sultanate of Oman' shapes from 1744 to 1814 (shapes.csv lists Tanzania and Kenya) and a separate row from 1814; the state is older than 1814 (Fort Jesus 1696-1698), so the sultanate-of-oman dossier should carry the African coast to 1813 or this dossier should be given an earlier start; no page opened dates the 1814 split (found event at confidence 1). (2) The 1840-1855 shape (185,340 km2) reaches 14.6 S in Mozambique and Cape Guardafui in Somalia; the Omani Empire page puts the southern limit 12 miles south of the Ruvuma and the Banadir as a nominal dependency. The keyframes are corrected to the strip plus a Banadir vassal tint (1828; reviewer af-05 moved it from 1843). (3) Mombasa: the Mombasa page has Omani rule restored in 1826 with liwalis (and the infobox Mombasa under Zanzibar from 1826) but also a 'nominal' annexation on 24 June 1837; the Said bin Sultan page has the conquest in 1837 and the Fort Jesus page local rule from 1741 to 1837; the dossier draws a vassal tint from 25 July 1826 and annexation on 24 June 1837, and the Mazrui town outside the direct shape until then (the sultanate-of-mombasa dossier of this batch carries the Mazrui side). (4) Capital: Zanzibar from 1832 (Omani Empire infobox) or 1840 (Said bin Sultan page); 1840 used. (5) End: Said's death is 19 October 1856 on the Said bin Sultan infobox but his reign is said to end 4 June 1856 in its lead; the 19 October 1856 division date is the Sultanate of Zanzibar infobox's.

Not covered by any page opened (left out, not filled from memory): the Omani hold on Kilwa and the Mrima coast before 1856, on Lamu and Pate before 1843, the Moresby (1822) and Hamerton (1845) treaties are slave-trade treaties and move no border, Mafia and Pemba are inside the Cliopatria shape without a dated acquisition. The pages are on a 5-page budget (Omani Empire, Said bin Sultan, Sultanate of Zanzibar, Mombasa, Pate Sultanate) plus the thin Mazrui article.

Gazetteer names needed: Pate (island and town), Siyu, Faza, Cape Delgado, Mafia Island; the Pate Island zone is a 35 km radius at 2.08 S, 41.10 E.
Counterparts needing dossiers: sultanate-of-mombasa and pate-sultanate (written in this batch), sultanate-of-oman (me-10: should record the 1856 division and the annual tribute Zanzibar owed Muscat), the Sultanate of the Geledi (Mogadishu hinterland, unwritten).
